title: Musher Blueprint Document
description: A composition of one or more components into a single deployable application.
$comment: Structural and type validation only — cross-document reference resolution, slug/directory agreement, and platform capability checks are separate validation layers. See spec.md.

kind.description: Document kind discriminator. Must be BLUEPRINT.

specVersion.description: Version of the Musher specification this document is written against.

BlueprintComputeConstraints.$comment: Every term pin is a lowercase token rather than a member of a closed set: the grammar is fixed by this contract, the vocabularies are not published anywhere yet, and spec.md §4.4 records that as a gap. cpuDedication is the exception — two values are the whole concept.
BlueprintComputeConstraints.description: Advanced, optional compute pins that narrow the hosts a node may be placed on. A pin never changes the compute the node's size names. See spec.md §4.4.

acceleratorInterconnect.description: Required accelerator interconnect, such as nvlink or pcie. Null pins nothing. The permitted terms are not a vocabulary this contract defines — see spec.md §4.4.

acceleratorRuntimes.description: Required accelerator runtimes, such as cuda. An empty array pins nothing, and a term may not repeat. The permitted terms are not a vocabulary this contract defines — see spec.md §4.4.

acceleratorSKUClass.description: Exact accelerator SKU class to pin. Null pins nothing. The permitted terms are not a vocabulary this contract defines — see spec.md §4.4.

cpuArchitectures.description: Permitted CPU architectures, such as x86_64 or arm64. An empty array pins nothing, and a term may not repeat. The permitted terms are not a vocabulary this contract defines — see spec.md §4.4.

cpuDedication.description: Whether the node's vCPU must be dedicated rather than shared. Null pins nothing. This is the one pin whose vocabulary this contract closes — see spec.md §4.4.

minAcceleratorMemoryGiB.description: Minimum accelerator VRAM in GiB. Null pins no floor.

minStorageIOPS.description: Minimum provisioned IOPS. Null pins no floor.

networkClass.description: Required network class. Null pins nothing. The permitted terms are not a vocabulary this contract defines — see spec.md §4.4.

storageClass.description: Required storage class, such as local-nvme. Null pins nothing. The permitted terms are not a vocabulary this contract defines — see spec.md §4.4.

BlueprintConnection.description:
A consumer-anchored wire (map value; keyed by the consumer input key).

The value names only the producer end (``fromRole`` / ``fromOutput``); the
consumer end is derived from the enclosing node (the node name) and the map
key (the input it fills). At most one wire per consumer input — the map key
makes that structural.

fromOutput.description: Declared output key on the producer component.

fromRole.description: Node name of the producer component.

BlueprintMetadata.description: Identity block of a blueprint document. The same shape carries on the sibling listing document, and the two must agree.

revision.description: Item revision — must agree between blueprint.yaml and listing.yaml.

slug.description: Item slug — must equal the item's directory name.

BlueprintNode.description:
One node of the blueprint's graph, keyed by node name.

A node places one component document — named by ``componentRef`` — onto a
compute ``size``, with optional host constraints (``placement``) and inbound
wires (``connections``).

The form of ``componentRef`` selects how it resolves: a reference beginning
``./`` or ``../`` names a document in the same repository, and one shaped
like a UUID names a published component and additionally requires
``revision``. See spec.md §4.1.

componentRef.$comment: Both patterns are lookahead-free so they compile under RE2 as well as ECMA-262. A path segment must begin with a letter or digit, which is how `.` and `..` are excluded as interior segments without a negative lookahead; that leaves one spelling per target and keeps the containment check in the semantic phase from having to normalise first.
componentRef.description: Reference to the component document this node deploys, in one of two forms. A repo-local reference begins ./ or ../ and ends .yaml or .yml, and resolves relative to the directory holding this blueprint document; its version is the referenced document's metadata.revision. A published reference is the component's UUID and requires revision. The relative-path prefix is what tells the two apart — a bare slug is not distinguishable from a UUID.

connections.description: Inbound wires for this node, keyed by the consumer input key each fills (value names the producer role and output; one wire per input).

propertyNames.$comment: spec.md §4.2 / ADR 0007 §4. A connection key IS an input name — §4.2 makes the map key the input being filled — so it takes the input grammar rather than one of its own.

placement.description: Optional placement compute pins that narrow the eligible-host set at schedule time. Absent, null, and a block with no pin set all mean the same thing. See spec.md §4.4.

revision.description: Lineage version pinned by a published reference. Required on a published reference and rejected on a repo-local one, where the referenced document's own metadata.revision supplies it.

size.$comment: Lookahead-free, so it compiles under RE2 as well as ECMA-262. Only the grammar is here. Which profiles are actually offered changes when the platform gains hardware to back a tier, not when this schema is released, so membership is a capability check rather than an enum. See spec.md §4.3.
size.description: Compute Profile slug bound to this node, in family.tier.size form — for example general.standard.small. Required per node, because a component document carries no compute of its own. The grammar is fixed here; the profiles actually on offer are published at https://api.musher.dev/v1/reference/compute-profiles.

BlueprintParameter.$comment: spec.md §5.3: a generated value is secret material, and sensitive is required explicitly because its default is false — the wrong answer here. The derived path inherits the marking from the input, which component §6.1 already obliges; this keeps the authored path from being the way to lose it. A platformDefault is forbidden beside a generator for the same reason it is on an input: minting a value and deriving one are two answers to one question. Mirrors ComponentInput's generator branch.
BlueprintParameter.description: An install-form parameter composed at the graph layer (map value; keyed by key).

description.description: Help text shown beneath the field, or null when none is set.

generator.description: Auto-generation spec when the platform mints the value at deploy time, or null when the deploying user supplies it.

platformDefault.description: Default the platform supplies when the deploying user does not; null when it does not supply one. A SELF_ADDRESS default resolves against each node this parameter covers.

required.description: True when the deploying user must provide a value before deploying.

schema.description: Data contract of the value: type, format, pattern, enum, default, sensitivity.

ui.description: Presentation metadata for the install form.

byteLength.description: Number of random bytes generated for the value.

charset.description: Explicit character set for the generated value, or null when the encoding default is used.

encoding.description: Encoding applied to the random bytes: HEX, BASE64, BASE64URL, or ALPHANUMERIC.

BlueprintParameterUi.$comment: spec.md §5.3, the block component §6.4 defines. The control is derived from the value's schema rather than declared, so this carries only what a derivation cannot supply.
BlueprintParameterUi.description: Presentation metadata for an install-form parameter.

enumLabels.description: Human-readable label for each enum member, keyed by the member it names. A member left unlabelled is offered as it is spelled.

examples.description: Example values illustrating the form a value takes. Never submitted — a value that is actually submitted is schema.default.

label.description: Human-readable label shown on the install form.

order.description: Relative position of the field within the form. Lower sorts first; a parameter declaring no order sorts after every parameter that declares one.

prominence.description: Standing of the field in the form: PRIMARY is offered directly, SECONDARY behind a disclosure the deploying user opens.

allOf.$comment: spec.md §5.3, the block component §6.3 defines. A JSON value's string form is a JSON document, and one value has many spellings — insignificant whitespace, member order, number formatting. `pattern` and `enum` both decide membership on the spelling, so neither can state a rule about the value.

spec.md §5.3, the block component §6.3 defines. Every `format` member names a lexical convention for text, so the field only refines a STRING. `type` is REQUIRED, so this is a `not` inside the `if` rather than an `else`: a document omitting `type` already reports ERR_MISSING_FIELD and should not also collect a format diagnostic.

BlueprintParameterValueSchema.description: Data contract of an install-form parameter value (JSON-Schema subset).

default.description: Pre-filled value, or null when the deploying user must supply one.

enum.description: Allowed values when the value is a closed enumeration; empty when unconstrained. MUST be empty where the type is JSON.

format.description: Semantic refinement of a STRING value: EMAIL, URI, ENDPOINT_URL, CONNECTION_STRING, HOSTNAME, or TIMEZONE; null when unrefined. MUST be null where the type is not STRING. Component spec.md §6.3 names where each convention is published.

pattern.description: Regular expression the supplied value must match, or null when unconstrained. MUST be null where the type is JSON.

sensitive.description: True when the value is secret material: masked in UIs, never echoed back.

type.description: Shape of the value's string form: STRING is any text, NUMBER a JSON number, BOOLEAN true or false, JSON a JSON document of any kind.

BlueprintPlatformDefault.$comment: spec.md §5.3, the block component §6.1 defines. `type` names the kind of default and is REQUIRED rather than defaulted, so a discriminator a document may omit is not one two implementations may read differently.
BlueprintPlatformDefault.description: Default the platform supplies when the deploying user does not. Which endpoint a SELF_ADDRESS default derives from is named rather than assumed, because component spec.md §5.2 permits more than one PUBLIC endpoint.

endpoint.description: Name of the PUBLIC endpoint the value is derived from. Null selects the primary endpoint component spec.md §5.2 elects.

source.description: What is derived. PUBLIC_HOSTNAME for the endpoint's hostname alone and PUBLIC_URL for its full URL, both from the URL an HTTP-family endpoint publishes; PUBLIC_ADDRESS for the full host:port and PUBLIC_PORT for the port alone, both from the edge address a TCP or UDP endpoint publishes.

type.description: Kind of default. SELF_ADDRESS derives the value from the covered node's own public addressing.

BlueprintSpec.description:
The ``spec`` block of a blueprint document.

An empty ``parameters`` map means the install-form parameters are derived
from the graph's merged USER-supplied inputs — the standard path. A
non-empty map is an authored override, used verbatim.

components.description: Component references composing the graph, keyed by graph-local node name. The name is what a connection's fromRole refers to and what the parameter merge orders the graph by; it means nothing outside this document. At least one node is required — spec.md §1 makes a blueprint a composition of one or more components, and an empty graph deploys nothing.

parameters.description: Authored install-form parameter overrides, keyed by parameter key. Empty means the parameters are derived from the graph's merged USER-supplied inputs.

propertyNames.$comment: spec.md §4 / ADR 0007 §4. An input, output and parameter name is lowerCamelCase: it is bound by key across three documents — the input, the connection key that fills it, and the parameter that covers it — and it is read by a person in an install form. Kebab-case survives neither the binding nor a generated SDK type without a translation nobody has to write today.
